We study the behavior in time of a subsystem (quantum harmonic oscillator) in contact, via an interaction Hamiltonian, with a reservoir (finite set (finite number of) uncoupled quantum harmonic oscillators).
the quantum Brownian motion is a non-equilibrium process, and that the subsystem mean occupation number does not decay to zero in the limit of large bath.

i) the eigenvalue problem of a quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a finite set of oscillators can be solved exactly; ii) we have obtained the temporal evolution of all the observables of interest; iii) we have studied the relaxation of the subsystem to the equilibrium state; iv) we have studied how the subsystem goes back to the initial state after a Poincar\'{e} recurrence time; v) the mean occupation number of the subsystem in the limit of large bath size decays
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a quantum system in contact with a reservoir of harmonic oscillators.
the dynamics of open quantum systems, and more precisely with the quantum Brownian motion.
the study of the quantum dynamics of a harmonic oscillator in contact with a finite set of oscillators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quantum Brownian motion is a good model for the study of the dynamics of a subsystem interacting with a thermal reservoir.
quantum Brownian motion is not a Markov process.
quantum Brownian motion is a very interesting and useful model to study the behavior of open quantum systems, but it is also a very complex model to analyze and to understand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subsystem goes to the equilibrium state with the same exponential rate as a free subsystem, but with a different equilibrium state.
the quantum Brownian motion is a quantum system that is not ergodic.
we have solved the problem of quantum Brownian motion exactly for a finite number of oscillators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subsystem goes to the equilibrium state, but it does so in a very peculiar way.
the subsystem mean occupation number does not decay exponentially in time, even in the limit of an infinite bath.
the subsystem mean occupation number does not necessarily decay exponentially with the number of bath oscillators, but rather it decays polynomially in the bath size.
